claim_text: Atlassian opened a Bitbucket status incident at 10:19 AM ET on Nov 23 for failing OAuth token requests
summary: Atlassian's Bitbucket status page opened an incident, 'Authentication service degraded', at 10:19 AM ET (15:19 UTC) on Nov 23. OAuth token requests may fail or time out. It was marked resolved at 3:44 PM ET the same day.
detail: The status page lists updates at 10:19 AM (investigating), 11:08 AM (cause identified), 11:33 AM (mitigation applied, monitoring) and 11:57 AM ET. Times are the status page's own, converted from UTC. Related services may be unavailable or degraded, it says.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Atlassian's own status page and its public incident feed give the incident, its start time and its state.

claim_text: The incident listed Authentication and user management and Pipelines as partial outages; the Bitbucket website, API and Git access showed operational
summary: The incident covered two Bitbucket components, Authentication and user management and Pipelines, both partial outages while it was open. The website, API, Git and webhooks showed operational. Both components were operational on Nov 24.
detail: A partial outage is Atlassian's term for part of a service being affected. The summary page at an earlier read listed only Authentication as degraded, so the Pipelines listing may have been added after the first post. The same incident also appears on Atlassian's Jira, Jira Service Management, Trello and Developer status pages; Atlassian's main status hub listed no incident at our check.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The component states are read straight from Atlassian's public status feed.

claim_text: Developers who log in through Atlassian sign-in or use Bitbucket Pipelines are the people affected
summary: The failing step is OAuth sign-in, shared by Bitbucket, Jira, Jira Service Management, Trello and Confluence, so it reaches people who sign in to those tools. CircleCI and FireHydrant reported knock-on failures on their own status pages.
detail: Atlassian has not said how many customers or regions are affected.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Atlassian describes the failing sign-in service on several product status pages; CircleCI and FireHydrant, independent companies, report knock-on failures on their own status pages. Who exactly was hit is not sized by any source.
notes: The CircleCI post is timed 2:51 PM UTC by the aggregator page, a few minutes before Atlassian opened its incident, and the aggregator may show a shifted clock. The press note that reports began at 9:53 AM ET comes from Downdetector, a user-report tracker.

claim_text: Users reported Bitbucket problems before Atlassian posted an incident
summary: An Australian outlet reports that Downdetector flagged Bitbucket problems from 9:53 AM ET, and that the Bitbucket status page still read all systems operational late in the morning. Atlassian opened its incident at 10:19 AM ET.
detail: The outlet's page was written while the status page was still clear; Atlassian's incident page now shows the 10:19 AM start. Downdetector counts user reports, which can spike for local reasons.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet relays a user-report tracker; Atlassian's own timestamp is the later start. We have not seen Downdetector's data directly.

claim_text: Atlassian has said the Bitbucket and sign-in problem was a hack
summary: Atlassian has not said the problem was an attack. Its status page names no cause and does not use the words attack, breach or hack.
detail: The status page says only that Atlassian has 'identified the cause' and is working on a mitigation.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Nothing on the status page or feed points to a security cause, and no source says Atlassian ruled one out either.
notes: Re-checked at 12:36 PM ET on the Bitbucket, Jira, Jira Service Management, Trello and Developer status pages: none names a cause or mentions an attack. Re-checked on Nov 24 after the incident was resolved: the closing update names no cause and does not mention an attack.

claim_text: Anyone has claimed responsibility for the Bitbucket and sign-in outage
summary: We found no claim of responsibility and no report from an outside researcher, authority or news outlet saying the outage was an attack.
detail: Outlets we found describe it only as an outage and describe user reports.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The sources describe a service failure and make no mention of an attacker.

summary: Atlassian said at 11:08 AM ET that it had identified the cause, and at 11:33 AM ET that it had applied a mitigation. It has not said what the cause is. The closing update at 3:44 PM ET does not name it either.
detail: The 10:19 AM post said Atlassian was still working to identify a resolution. We found no post-incident report.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The status page's updates name no cause.

summary: Atlassian gives no number of affected customers or regions.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The status page does not size the impact.

claim_text: Atlassian said at 11:08 AM ET that it had identified the cause and was working on a mitigation
summary: Atlassian's second status update, at 11:08 AM ET (16:08 UTC), says it has identified the cause, teams are working on a mitigation, and affected users may see requests fail or time out.
detail: This confirms what Atlassian said, not an independent finding. The update does not say what the cause is.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The wording is on Atlassian's own incident page and public feed.

claim_text: Atlassian said at 11:33 AM ET that it had applied a mitigation and was seeing signs of recovery
summary: At 11:33 AM ET (16:33 UTC) Atlassian moved the incident to monitoring: a mitigation was applied and services showed signs of recovery. It repeated this up to 12:32 PM ET. Some users may still see errors or timeouts.
detail: This is Atlassian's own account of the recovery. The incident was not marked resolved at 12:36 PM ET. FireHydrant, a company that integrates with Jira, said at 11:42 AM ET that its Jira integration had recovered.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The monitoring updates are on Atlassian's own incident pages and public feed; FireHydrant's independent status page reports recovery on its side.

claim_text: The same authentication incident is posted on Atlassian's Jira, Jira Service Management, Trello, Developer and Confluence status pages
summary: Atlassian posted it for Jira (from 10:19 AM ET) and for Jira Service Management, Trello and its developer platform (from 11:08 AM ET). Confluence's page added it at 1:07 PM ET, dated from 10:19 AM, and moved it to monitoring at 1:10 PM.
detail: Trello lists its site, API and Atlassian's support portal as partial outages; Confluence lists Authentication and User Management as a partial outage. Confluence's page showed no incident at our 12:36 PM ET check. Atlassian's main status hub listed none at our 1:35 PM ET check.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Each product's own Atlassian status page carries the incident with its start time and affected components.

claim_text: Atlassian marked the incident resolved at 3:44 PM ET on Nov 23 and says the service is operating normally
summary: Atlassian's Bitbucket status page moved the incident to resolved at 3:44 PM ET (20:44 UTC) on Nov 23, about five and a half hours after it opened. It says the service is operating normally for all affected customers.
detail: Read on Nov 24: Authentication and user management and Pipelines both show operational, and the feed of unresolved incidents is empty. The closing update names no cause, and no post-incident report is attached.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The resolved state, its time and the closing wording are on Atlassian's own incident page and public feed.
